groups.title: Joining the reading club

dialogue.speaker: Mook
dialogue.text: Hey Daniel, are you still looking for people to help with the weekend reading club at the community centre?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Yes, we're still two tutors short. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Mook
dialogue.text: I might be. What exactly would I have to do?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: Mostly read with kids aged eight to ten and help them with new words. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Mook
dialogue.text: That sounds manageable. But I have extra maths classes every other Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: ___3___ Quite a few volunteers only come twice a month.

dialogue.speaker: Mook
dialogue.text: Great. Then count me in. Is there any training before we start?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There's a short session next Friday after school. ___4___

dialogue.speaker: Mook
dialogue.text: Sure, I'll be there.

options: Why, do you know anyone who might help?
Are you already one of our tutors?
Have you ever taught young children?
Why, are you interested in joining?
items.explanationTh: Mook ตอบว่า "I might be." แล้วถามว่าต้องทำอะไรบ้าง แสดงว่า Daniel ถามว่าเธอสนใจไหม (Are you interested…? → I might be.) ถ้าถามว่ารู้จักใครที่ช่วยได้ หรือเคยสอนเด็กไหม จะตอบว่า "I might be." ไม่ได้ และถ้าเป็นติวเตอร์อยู่แล้วเธอก็ไม่ต้องถามว่าต้องทำอะไร

options: It's about two hours every Saturday morning.
It pays quite well for a weekend job.
You'll need a teaching degree before you start.
It's mainly on weekday afternoons.
items.explanationTh: Mook ตอบว่างานพอทำได้ "but I have extra maths classes every other Saturday" จึงต้องเป็นข้อมูลเรื่องเวลาวันเสาร์ ส่วนงานวันธรรมดาไม่ชนกับเรียนวันเสาร์ งานอาสาไม่มีค่าจ้าง และการต้องมีปริญญาก็ไม่ "manageable"

options: In that case, I'm afraid you can't join.
That's not a problem at all.
You'd need to move them to Sundays, then.
Every Saturday is compulsory, though.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคต่อมาบอกว่าอาสาสมัครหลายคนมาแค่เดือนละสองครั้ง แสดงว่าการติดเรียนบางเสาร์ไม่เป็นปัญหา ส่วนการบอกว่าเข้าร่วมไม่ได้ ต้องย้ายวันเรียนพิเศษ หรือต้องมาทุกเสาร์ ขัดกับข้อมูลนี้

options: Would you rather skip the training?
Did you go to last month's session?
Could you make it at four o'clock?
Who will be running the session?
items.explanationTh: Mook ตอบว่า "Sure, I'll be there." ซึ่งเป็นการตอบรับคำถามว่าจะมาตามเวลาที่นัดได้ไหม การถามว่าอยากข้ามการอบรม เคยไปครั้งก่อนไหม หรือใครเป็นผู้จัด ตอบด้วยประโยคนี้ไม่ได้

dialogue.text: Let me check. The small rooms, which seat four, are free from one to three, but the large rooms are fully booked.

So nobody is allowed in the large rooms?

options: Could you spell your surname for me?
Shall I put you on the waiting list?
Could I have your student number?
How many hours will you need the room?
items.explanationTh: Krit ตอบด้วยตัวเลข "6402871" จึงเป็นการขอเลขประจำตัวนักศึกษา ส่วนจำนวนชั่วโมงทราบแล้ว (10 โมงถึงเที่ยง) และการสะกดนามสกุลหรือรายชื่อสำรองไม่ตอบเป็นตัวเลข

groups.title: A problem in the dorm laundry room

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: Have you been down to the laundry room today? Both washing machines are out of order.

dialogue.speaker: Toey
dialogue.text: Both of them? ___1___ They were only fixed last month.

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: I think someone overloaded them with heavy blankets.

dialogue.speaker: Toey
dialogue.text: ___2___ Should we put up a sign about not overloading them?

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: Good idea. But the dorm office says the repair person can't come until Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Toey
dialogue.text: ___3___ The laundry shop across the road is open until ten.

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: True. I'll take my school uniforms there tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Pim
dialogue.text: OK, I'll post a message in the dorm group chat right now.

options: I'm not surprised. They're ancient.
I know. I've just used one of them.
Seriously? That's so frustrating.
Good. I'd rather wash things by hand.
items.explanationTh: Toey พูดต่อว่า "They were only fixed last month." ซึ่งแสดงความแปลกใจและหงุดหงิด จึงต้องเป็น "Seriously? That's so frustrating." ส่วน "I'm not surprised" ขัดกับความแปลกใจนี้ การบอกว่าเพิ่งใช้เครื่องขัดกับที่เครื่องเสียทั้งสองเครื่อง และการดีใจที่จะได้ซักมือไม่เข้ากับการบ่นที่ตามมา

options: But they were empty when I checked.
That sounds quite likely, actually.
I doubt it. They're built for that.
Then it must be a power problem.
items.explanationTh: Toey เสนอต่อทันทีให้ติดป้ายห้ามใส่ผ้ามากเกินไป แสดงว่าเขาเห็นด้วยกับสาเหตุที่ Pim บอก จึงตอบว่า "That sounds quite likely" ส่วนการแย้งว่าเครื่องว่างอยู่ ไม่เชื่อว่าเป็นสาเหตุ หรือคิดว่าเป็นปัญหาไฟฟ้า จะไม่นำไปสู่การติดป้ายเรื่องใส่ผ้ามากเกินไป

options: That's not the end of the world.
Then we'll just have to wait till then.
So nobody can do any washing this week.
In that case, I'll have to go home to wash.
items.explanationTh: Toey เสนอทางออกต่อทันทีว่าร้านซักผ้าฝั่งตรงข้ามเปิดถึงสี่ทุ่ม แสดงว่าการรอช่างถึงวันพฤหัสไม่ใช่ปัญหาใหญ่ "That's not the end of the world." ส่วนการต้องรอ ซักไม่ได้ทั้งสัปดาห์ หรือต้องกลับไปซักที่บ้าน ขัดกับทางออกที่เสนอ

options: Could you take a few of my school shirts, too?
Let's keep this to ourselves for now.
Let's warn everyone else on our floor, too.
Shall we ask the office for a refund?
items.explanationTh: Pim ตอบว่าจะโพสต์ข้อความในกลุ่มแชตของหอทันที แสดงว่า Toey เสนอให้แจ้งเพื่อนคนอื่น ส่วน "keep this to ourselves" ขัดกับการโพสต์บอกทุกคน และการฝากเสื้อหรือขอเงินคืนไม่ได้รับคำตอบเป็นการโพสต์ในกลุ่มแชต

groups.title: An internship interview at a radio station

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Hello, you must be Phum. Sorry, our morning meeting ran over. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: Only a few minutes, and I enjoyed listening to the live show in reception.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: That's good to hear. So, why would you like to spend your summer at River City Radio?

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: I'm planning to study communication arts, and I'd like to understand ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Fair enough. Have you done any broadcasting before?

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: A little. I present the morning announcements at school every Monday. ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: So you're used to speaking to a large audience. ___4___

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: I try to stay calm. Once, the microphone stopped working, so I simply spoke louder until a teacher fixed the cable.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Good thinking. ___5___ Most of our interns spend their days editing audio and checking facts for the news team.

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: That suits me. ___6___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Excellent. We've had problems with careless mistakes in the past. The internship lasts six weeks from the 9th of June. How does that sound?

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: ___7___ Would it be possible to start a week later?

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: I think we can manage that, as long as you stay a week longer at the end.

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: That would be perfect. Could I ask one more thing? ___8___

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Yes. If you're shortlisted, we'll ask you to record a two-minute news bulletin, so it's worth practising reading aloud.

dialogue.speaker: Phum
dialogue.text: Then I'll start practising tonight. Thank you very much.

dialogue.speaker: Ms Rivera
dialogue.text: Thank you, Phum. It was nice to meet you.

options: Have you been to a radio station before?
Did you manage to find a parking space?
Would you like to come back another day?

groups.title: Photography workshop
groups.text:
LIGHT & SHADOW: A Weekend Photography Workshop
Fernhill Arts Centre, Chiang Mai

Tired of photos that look nothing like what you actually saw? Join award-winning photographer Dara Venn for two days of hands-on learning designed for beginners and improvers aged 15 and above.

Day 1 (Saturday): Understanding light — composition, exposure and why the "golden hour" matters, followed by an afternoon photo walk through the old city.
Day 2 (Sunday): Editing without overdoing it — we use free software only, so there are no expensive subscriptions to buy.

Bring any camera you own; a smartphone is perfectly acceptable. Laptops are provided on Day 2.

Dates: 14–15 March, 9:00–16:00
Fee: 1,800 baht (lunch included). Students with a valid ID pay 1,400 baht.

Places are limited to 12 participants so that everyone receives individual feedback. Register by 7 March at fernhillarts.example. Anyone who registers by 28 February will also receive a free printed copy of their best photo from the weekend.

items.stem: Who is the workshop mainly intended for?
options: Children under 15 who are learning to use a camera
Designers who want to create their own editing software
People who want to develop their basic photography skills
Professional photographers who hope to win awards
items.explanationTh: โฆษณาระบุว่า "designed for beginners and improvers aged 15 and above" คือผู้เริ่มต้นและผู้ที่ต้องการพัฒนาฝีมือ ไม่ใช่มืออาชีพหรือเด็กอายุต่ำกว่า 15 ปี

items.stem: What does the advertisement say about equipment?

Participants must pay for editing software.
Participants should bring a professional camera.
A phone camera is good enough to take part.

be unable to join because registration has closed.

groups.text:
SECOND LIFE ELECTRONICS — Repair, Refurbish, Reuse

Before you throw away that cracked phone or silent speaker, bring it to us. Since 2019, our team of six technicians has given more than 15,000 devices a second life.

What we do
• Screen and battery replacement for phones and tablets (most jobs finished within two hours)
• Laptop repairs, including keyboards, cooling fans and charging ports
• Refurbished devices for sale, each checked on 30 points and sold with a six-month warranty

How it works
1. Bring your device in for a free check.
2. We give you a fixed price before any work begins — no hidden costs.
3. If we can't fix it, you pay nothing.

Trade-in offer: Hand in any old device, working or not, and get 10% off a refurbished one. Devices that cannot be repaired are passed on to a certified recycling partner.

Open Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00–19:00 | 88/4 Wiang Road, Ban Khlong Sai

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this advertisement?
options: To explain how customers can repair their own phones at home
To recruit experienced technicians for its growing repair team

groups.text:
Ledgestone Climbing Hall, Beginners' Course — 4 out of 5 stars
Reviewed by Tonkla, Grade 11

I had never climbed anything taller than a school fence, so I signed up for Ledgestone's four-week beginners' course feeling rather nervous. After eight sessions, I can honestly say it was one of the best decisions I made this year.

The instructors are the course's greatest strength. Before anyone touched a wall, we spent the whole first session learning to tie knots and check each other's equipment, and the instructors then checked every knot again themselves. They were patient with slow learners like me and never made anyone feel embarrassed for coming down early.

The hall itself is bright and well organised. The easier walls are kept apart from the advanced area, so beginners are not distracted by experienced climbers. Shoes and harnesses are included in the course fee, which means you do not have to buy expensive gear before you know whether you even like the sport.

The course costs 2,400 baht. After that, a single visit costs 200 baht, or you can buy a ten-visit card for 1,600 baht.

My one real complaint is the changing area. There are only two showers for the whole hall, and on weekday evenings the queue is long enough to put you off coming back.

Overall, if you have ever been curious about climbing, this course is a safe and friendly place to start. Just try to book a weekend morning slot.

groups.text:
Pottery Find Puts School Sports Field on Hold

BAN NA KHAM, 14 August — Work on a new sports field at Ban Na Kham Secondary School has been put on hold after a digger uncovered pieces of ancient pottery last Tuesday.

The fragments, found about a metre below the surface, include parts of at least three large storage jars decorated with a simple rope pattern. Archaeologists from Khao Sung University, who visited the site on Thursday, believe the jars may be around 2,000 years old, although laboratory tests will be needed to confirm this.

"Pieces like these suggest that people were living, or at least storing food, on this spot long before the village existed," said Dr Anong Pakdee, who is leading the team. "The next few weeks should tell us whether this was a single household or a larger settlement."

The university team will carry out a careful excavation during the school's October break, when no classes are held. Students in Grades 10 to 12 have been invited to join as volunteers, working in small groups under the supervision of trained staff.

The delay means that the football field, which was due to open in November, is now expected to be completed in February at the earliest. Some parents have expressed disappointment, since the school's teams currently have to train at a public park three kilometres away.

Head teacher Surasak Inthawong, however, sees an opportunity. "Our students can now study history in the place where it happened," he said. "That is worth waiting a few extra months for." He added that, if the site proves important, the school hopes to display some of the finds in its library.

groups.title: Why We Put Things Off
groups.text:
Why We Put Things Off

Almost everyone has experienced it. An important assignment is due in three days, yet you find yourself reorganising your bookshelf, watching cooking videos or suddenly deciding that your desk drawer urgently needs cleaning. Procrastination, the voluntary delay of a task despite knowing that the delay will probably make things worse, is often treated as a sign of laziness. Many psychologists, however, now argue that this view misses the point. Procrastination, they say, is less a problem of managing time than a problem of managing emotions.

According to this emotional view, people delay tasks not because they are unwilling to work but because the task itself triggers unpleasant feelings. An essay might bring on anxiety about being judged; a complicated application form might cause confusion or simple boredom. Avoiding the task offers immediate relief from these feelings. The trouble is that the relief is temporary. The deadline does not move, and the negative feelings usually return, stronger than before and often joined by guilt.

Researchers have described this pattern as a conflict between the "present self" and the "future self". Some studies suggest that when people think about themselves in the future, their brains respond in a way that looks surprisingly similar to when they think about strangers. In other words, we tend to treat the person who will face tomorrow's deadline as someone else, someone who will somehow have more energy, more time and more motivation than we do now. Handing the job over to that person feels perfectly reasonable in the moment.

Perfectionism can make matters worse. Students who set extremely high standards for themselves are, perhaps surprisingly, often among the most serious procrastinators. If a piece of work must be flawless, starting it becomes threatening, because every early draft is a reminder of how far it falls short. Delaying the task protects the perfectionist from that discomfort. It also provides a convenient excuse if the final result is poor: "I only had one night to do it."

If procrastination is mainly emotional, then simply buying a planner or downloading a productivity app is unlikely to solve it. Instead, psychologists recommend strategies that make starting less painful. One is to reduce the first step to something so small that it seems almost ridiculous, such as "open the document and type the title". Once people begin, they often find the task less unpleasant than they had imagined, and continuing becomes easier. Another strategy is to remove temptations in advance, for instance by leaving a phone in another room, so that avoiding work requires more effort than doing it.

Perhaps the most unexpected recommendation is self-forgiveness. Researchers have reported, for example, that students who forgave themselves for putting off revision before one exam tended to procrastinate less before the next. Being harsh on oneself, it seems, simply adds another bad feeling that people then try to escape.

None of this means that deadlines and schedules are useless. But understanding procrastination as a problem of mood rather than a flaw in character changes the question we ask. Instead of "Why am I so lazy?", a more useful question may be "What feeling am I trying to avoid right now?"

groups.title: Bridges That Bend Without Breaking
groups.text:
Bridges That Bend Without Breaking

A large bridge looks like the very picture of stability: tons of steel and concrete stretching calmly across a river or valley. Yet every bridge is constantly moving. Traffic makes it vibrate, changes in temperature cause it to expand and shrink, and wind and earthquakes push it with forces that can be far greater than the weight of the vehicles on top. Modern bridge design is therefore not about making structures completely rigid, but about controlling how they move.

Wind is a particular challenge for long, light bridges such as suspension bridges. When wind flows past a bridge deck, it can create swirling patterns of air on alternate sides of the structure. If these swirls push the deck at a rhythm that matches the rate at which the bridge naturally vibrates, known as its natural frequency, the movements can grow larger with each cycle, much as a child on a swing goes higher with well-timed pushes. This effect, called resonance, can turn a steady breeze into a serious threat.

To prevent this, engineers test scale models in wind tunnels long before construction begins. A model of the deck, often only a few metres long, is exposed to winds of different speeds and directions while sensors record how it responds. The results frequently lead to changes in the shape of the deck. Many modern decks have a streamlined cross-section, similar to an aircraft wing, which allows air to flow smoothly past instead of breaking into swirls. Others include open grates or small fins that disrupt the regular pattern of air before it can build up.

Earthquakes present a different problem. Instead of acting mainly on the deck, they shake the ground beneath the bridge, sending sudden forces up through its foundations and towers. A structure that is too stiff may crack, because it cannot absorb this energy. One common solution is to place special bearings between the deck and its supports. These bearings, typically made of alternating layers of rubber and steel, allow the ground to move sideways beneath the bridge while the deck itself moves much less. In effect, the bridge is partly separated from the shaking earth.

Engineers also add devices called dampers, which work in a similar way to the shock absorbers in a car. Dampers convert the energy of movement into heat, reducing the size of vibrations whether they are caused by wind, earthquakes or even large crowds of pedestrians. Some very long bridges contain enormous tuned mass dampers: heavy blocks mounted on springs that are designed to swing against the bridge's own motion and so cancel part of it.

None of these features can make a bridge completely safe from every possible event, and all of them add to construction costs. However, inspections carried out after major earthquakes have repeatedly shown that bridges fitted with bearings and dampers suffer far less damage than older bridges without them. For this reason, many countries now require such protection for new bridges in high-risk areas and are gradually upgrading older ones.

So the next time you cross a long bridge and feel a slight movement beneath your feet, there is no need to panic. That movement is not a sign of weakness. More often, it is evidence that the bridge is doing exactly what its designers intended: bending a little so that it does not break.
